Resized Current-Flow Betweenness

Source: R/centrality-batch69.R
centrality_rcfb.Rd

RCFB (Agryzkov et al. 2019) joins every node to a virtual target by a link of conductance \(\varepsilon\), lets one unit of current enter at each node \(s\) in turn, and credits the current of every edge to its end of higher potential: $$b_i = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{s} \sum_{j:\, u^{(s)}_i > u^{(s)}_j} q_{ij} \bigl(u^{(s)}_i - u^{(s)}_j\bigr), \qquad u^{(s)} = (\varepsilon I + L)^{-1} e_s,$$ with \(q_{ij}\) the conductance (weight) of the edge \(ij\), \(L\) the weighted Laplacian and \(n\) the number of nodes.

Usage

centrality_rcfb(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses rcfb_epsilon (default 0, the limit) and the edge weights (weighted).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The source defines the measure on undirected networks with edge weights as conductances; a weight is read as a conductance (for a resistance, give its reciprocal) and loops are ignored. A network with an arc whose reverse is missing or has another weight has no value: the measure warns (class cograph_undefined_measure) and returns NA. The source bounds \(\varepsilon\) above by one over the sum of the edge resistances (its equation 14) and gives no value. rcfb_epsilon = 0, the default, takes the limit \(\varepsilon \to 0\) (owner decision 2026-11-26), in which the potential differences are those of the Laplacian pseudo-inverse; on the Krackhardt kite \(\varepsilon = 10^{-6}\) is within \(10^{-6}\) of it. A positive rcfb_epsilon at or above the bound raises a cograph_bad_parameter error. The network need not be connected: the current of a source stays in its component, and an isolated node scores 0.

The loop of the source's Algorithm 2 credits every edge, also those at the source, so a source is credited with the current it sends out; that is the second option of its equation (19), \(I_s = x_s - x_s/n\), and it is what is computed (a builder choice). The caption of Algorithm 2 names the first option, \(I_s = 0\); in the limit that reading subtracts \((1 - 1/n_c)/n\) from every score, \(n_c\) the size of the node's component, so it ranks the nodes of one component in the same order. Algorithm 2 also omits the conductance of equation (18), which matters only on a weighted network; the current includes it here. The source prints no score. The implementation reproduces the values a source audit computed on the Krackhardt kite in the limit (10 of 10) and its distances to the limit at \(\varepsilon = 10^{-4}\) and \(10^{-6}\); the audit's ten values at \(\varepsilon = 1\), which is above the bound, are reproduced by the internal computation, which this function does not let reach that value. On four test networks the score ranks nodes closest to centrality_current_flow_betweenness (mean Kendall correlation 0.958, 0.931 at the least) and centrality_godfather (0.87); with centrality_betweenness the correlation is 0.83 to 0.87. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Agryzkov, T., Tortosa, L. and Vicent, J. F. (2019). A variant of the current flow betweenness centrality and its application in urban networks. Applied Mathematics and Computation, 347, 600-615. doi:10.1016/j.amc.2018.11.032 .

See also

centrality_current_flow_betweenness, centrality_betweenness, centrality.

Examples

centrality_rcfb(to_undirected(regulation_net))
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>  0.1318329  0.1491990  0.1432635  0.1681408  0.1516253  0.1464511  0.1026948 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>  0.1376961  0.1216454  0.1430690 
centrality_rcfb(to_undirected(regulation_net), weighted = FALSE, rcfb_epsilon = 1e-4)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>  0.1232380  0.1403001  0.1501619  0.1498074  0.1353150  0.1249504  0.1096086 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>  0.1187143  0.1349811  0.1172644
